sentence: This project studies how changing metabolism can trigger cell death in small cell lung cancer.
This project tries to find out what gets in the way of, and what helps, adults who use both e-cigarettes and cigarettes to cut harm.
This project studies how long-term HIV infection leads to worse diabetic kidney disease in patients.
This project uses large language models to sort errors in medical orders, such as imaging and medication orders.
This project uses machine learning with digital biomarkers to predict how a disease progresses in each patient.
This project tests whether brain stimulation with a weak electric current over the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex can reduce craving in people with cocaine use disorder.
This project studies how the network of mitochondria changes its shape and behavior over space and time.
This project uses genomic tools to find out why glioblastoma, a brain tumor, comes back after treatment.
This project tests chemical changes to double stranded RNAs to find out how they work.
This project tests whether a special scan can find clinically significant prostate cancer in patients on active surveillance.
This project builds a collection of tissue samples from anal cancer and cervical cancer patients for other cancer studies to use.
This project builds a low-cost tool that quickly detects illicit substances in urine samples.
This project builds a treatment that uses a plant virus injected into solid tumors to stimulate an immune response against them.
This project studies how the motions of nitric oxide synthase, a protein with several parts, relate to how it works.
This project records activity in brain regions for at least one month to learn how some memories are forgotten while others become stable.
This project provides computer and software support, including machine learning tools, for vision research laboratories.
This project uses position emission tomography imaging to study how chronic stress changes immune responses in cardiovascular disease.
This project studies how changes in the gut microbiome relate to immune recovery in children after stem cell transplant.
This project studies how Staphylococcus aureus bacteria hide inside host cells and survive antibiotics, to find ways to kill them.
